Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify staggered rollout window + enablement exceptions

Team —

Quick alignment ask before I confirm the final launch timing with EdgeCloud / Acme next week. Two points we need an internal decision on by EOD Friday:

1) Staggered rollout window: EdgeCloud wants a 2-week progressive ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to test performance across regions. Do we have capacity and rollback hooks for the middle step (50%) without the full observability suite enabled?

2) Enablement exceptions: the customer is requesting a condensed enablement deck and a shortened admin training (1 hour) due to their compressed calendar. This would require us to sign off on a limited docs deliverable and an SLA exception for training SLOs.

Notes:
- Launch branch is feature/edgecloud-v2; there are two minor doc gaps flagged in the tracker (localization and GV UI screenshots).
- Proposed canary plan attached as a matrix.

Please reply with: (a) thumbs up/down on the 2-week staged rollout, (b) whether we can accept the condensed enablement (and who owns the reduced deck), and (c) any operational blockers for pausing observability during step 2.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: canary-rollout-matrix.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify staggered rollout window + enablement exceptions

Kimberly —

Short answer: leaning NO on disabling parts of observability during the 50% step. Our current SLOs for telemetry ingestion are tied to alerting that will detect regressions in latency/cost quickly. If we reduce tracing/metrics we risk not catching a perf regression before it impacts customers.

However, a two-week progressive ramp is fine if we:
- Keep core latency/error metrics on (sampling can increase, but not stop).
- Require a pre-step smoke test in region staging with the EdgeCloud dataset (I can schedule this with infra).

On the condensed enablement: we can produce a 10-slide executive deck + 1-hour trainer script, but we need a doc owner. I can take the UI screenshots (Marcus). We will need Content to strip examples and mark the doc as "preview" for localized strings.

Blocking items: localization flags must be resolved (EN->FR/DE) or call out as "coming soon" in the deck.

-Marcus
Principal Product Manager

Kimberly / team —

I support the 2-week progressive ramp with conditions. Operational suggestions:
- Canary cohort 1 (10%): US-west customers only — run for 48 hours, automated rollback at 5% error increase or 30% latency tail.
- Cohort 2 (50%): only after two green 48h windows and signoff from CS and PM. Observe KV cache pressure metrics closely.

For the enablement ask, propose this compromise: we ship the condensed deck now and follow with a detailed "deep-dive" playbook at +2 weeks. That lets EdgeCloud go-live while keeping us covered for more complex cases. I can own the canary automation and will add health-check hooks to mitigate risk.

I'll need approval from Lauren on any SLA exceptions (training SLO) and for CS to commit a trainer.

- Aditya
Software Engineering Manager, Runtime

All —

I'm okay with the 2-week staged rollout under the conditions Marcus and Aditya listed: telemetry sampling remains, smoke tests complete, and CS/trainer commit in place. Approve the condensed enablement deck as a minimum viable delivery, provided we get a follow-up deep-dive playbook within 14 calendar days post-launch.

Action items I expect before I confirm with the customer:
- Aditya: automation + rollback thresholds and where the kill-switch sits.
- Marcus: screenshots + doc owner for the condensed deck (assign to Content & mark locale gaps).
- Tessa: schedule two 45-minute training slots within the first 7 days post-launch.

I will approve a one-time SLA exception for training length. Please route the SLA exception request to ops for tracking (attach the doc).

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
